newsitem.title: UK: Shield says heart attack test on target.
newsitem.headline: Shield says heart attack test on target.

text.p: Britain's Shield Diagnostics Plc said on Friday it was still on target to seek U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for its heart attack test in the summer. Shares in the company were up 40 pence at 437 1/2 at 1515 GMT after touching a high of 455 pence.

In a statement Shield said it remained confident about the efficacy of its test for Activated Factor Twelve (AFT) in predicting propensity to cardiovascular disease and heart attacks, "and the company's ability to commercialise the product in conjunction with others".
The company attacked "a series of ill-informed technical commentaries on AFT and Shield."

Nervousness among investors has set Shield's shares on a roller-coaster ride this year, dropping back to current levels from a brief high of 928 pence earlier this year. The company has been criticised for the way in which it has presented information about its diagnostic product for AFT, which it hopes will be a much more accurate predictor of heart attacks than cholesterol levels. "The fundamentals of Shield are in place to deliver value to shareholders over the medium term," the company said.
